evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Entering a name and optional description are attributes of a single 'create game' feature, not independent features.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: This describes one feature: inviting estimators via a URL.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Single actionable feature: starting a round by entering an item.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Viewing all items in the session is one feature.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item (for estimate or re-estimate) is a single selection feature; 're-estimated' is a usage variant rather than a separate feature.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item is one implementable feature.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item is a single feature.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item is one independent feature.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing all estimates immediately is a single behavior/feature.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting the average is a single decision/feature.

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling the estimate under a specific condition is one feature (with a condition), not multiple features.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering the agreed estimate is a single feature.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating a previously estimated story is one feature.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing from a spreadsheet is a single feature.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste import is one feature (a specific import mechanism).

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games is a single feature.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript is one feature.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting as HTML is a single export feature.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting as CSV is one discrete export feature (separate from HTML but itself atomic).

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game is a single action/feature.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Multiple input fields are attributes of the single 'create account' feature, not separate features.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in with credentials is one feature.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Updating account details is a single feature (with possibly multiple fields as attributes).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Account deletion is one feature.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Displaying dates/times in local timezone is a single feature.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder via email is one feature.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Choosing the estimation scale is a single configurable feature (enumerating options is attribute of that feature).

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Allowing invitations up to a limit is one feature (a single constraint).

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining a game by entering a name is a single feature.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Displaying the current item is one feature.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the session's items is a single feature (similar to PP-004 but still atomic).

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Notifying that a specific estimator has given an estimate is one feature.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Synchronous reveal of estimates after all have voted is a single feature.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Allowing estimate changes up to reveal is one controllable feature.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior estimates for the same story is a single feature.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Displaying which participant gave which estimate in the round is one feature.

evaluations.evidence: be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Starting a shared two-minute timer is a single feature.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Automatic reset behavior for the timer is a single feature (behavior of the timer).

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Ability to scroll back through prior rounds is one feature.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Ensuring consistent card ordering is a single UI/behavior requirement.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Allowing estimate changes before draw completion is one feature (similar to PP-034).

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail near cards is a single presentation feature.

evaluations.evidence: have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Compliance with XHTML and CSS is a single cross-cutting quality requirement (attributes of one compliance feature).

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing a glossary is one feature.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: Creating database indexes is a single backend optimization task/feature.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Specifying correct function across multiple distinct browsers enumerates multiple independently testable/prioritizable compatibility targets; these can be implemented and verified separately.

evaluations.evidence: have the site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a single cross-cutting quality feature.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance responsiveness is one non-functional requirement/feature.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Supporting Unicode is a single capability requirement.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Providing sensible/predictable URLs is one UX requirement.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Designing nice error pages is a single feature.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Anonymizing stored results is one privacy/data storage feature.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Providing usage metrics is a single analytic/feature request.
